review: Independent source, coverage and key challenge 02
scope: October 13, 2025 Law: common rules, four base factions, Autumn/Fall and Winter, Thief/Tinker/Ranger, dominance and coalition; expansion systems, second Vagabond, hirelings, landmarks, bots and Advanced Setup excluded.

method.source_read: Complete applicable numbered rules 1-9.6, applicable G.1-36, C.1, M.1-2, V.1-3, and page 32 reminder. PDF applicable-page text was compared directly to the extraction; all compared pages match after whitespace normalization. PDF page 9 was rendered and visually checked for item glyphs and allied-hit wording.
method.comparison_standard: Checked actual question wording and expected answers rather than accepting ledger passage labels. New questions require a distinct rule, outcome branch, or consequential timing/priority/exception; numeric variants and mechanical recombinations are rejected.

key_review.note: Broad answers are read with their explicitly tested faction exceptions. In particular, Q03 warrior-first removal does not override Vagabond item damage/allied-hit rules, and Q05 normal dominance conditions are paired with Q20 coalition rules.

rejected_candidates.candidate: Whether Vagabond can split hits between items and allied warriors rather than exhausting all allied warriors first
rejected_candidates.reason: The actual answers permit allied-warrior versus item damage comparison. Warrior-first in 4.3.6 prioritizes warriors over buildings/tokens, not over items. Asking a concrete split repeats that permission plus the already-tested strict comparison, rather than adding a rule.

rejected_candidates.candidate: Who pays Outrage when Vagabond forces Allied warriors to move
rejected_candidates.reason: The bank already tests forced actor identity/rules, the allied-warrior Outrage trigger and ordinary payment. A named-faction payer example is a mechanical recombination of those answers, with no source-specific exception.

rejected_candidates.candidate: A defenseless defender can still play an ambush
rejected_candidates.reason: Q03 grants the defender its ambush opportunity without a warrior requirement; Q68 limits attacking presence only. A concrete defenseless ambush scenario introduces no exception.

rejected_candidates.candidate: Attacker still deals counted hits after losing its last warrior in the Deal Hits step
rejected_candidates.reason: The keyed battle procedure counts/caps hits before Deal Hits; immediate battle ending for missing attackers is specifically placed after ambush. This would recombine the already-tested step order rather than add a rule.

rejected_candidates.candidate: Damaged face-down tea can refresh without being repaired
rejected_candidates.reason: The answers explicitly keep damage separate from readiness, allow Refresh without repairing and preserve faces on damage. Changing the item type does not add a branch.

rejected_candidates.candidate: Face-up track item remains in Satchel when its track is full
rejected_candidates.reason: The answer says move to an empty matching space only when able and gives track capacity three. The overflow branch follows directly from the actual conditional answer.

rejected_candidates.candidate: Crafted boot or tea may be used immediately by Vagabond
rejected_candidates.reason: Q56 explicitly tests immediate face-up use if otherwise eligible; item-specific examples repeat it.

rejected_candidates.candidate: Eyrie must battle a building-only enemy and may not skip an impossible Decree battle
rejected_candidates.reason: The bank gives Decree full completion, ordinary battle prerequisites and defenseless battle. This is a recombination, not a missing Eyrie exception.

rejected_candidates.candidate: Despot scores only one extra point for multiple buildings removed in one battle
rejected_candidates.reason: The actual answer says one extra VP when removing at least one enemy building/token in battle. Another removal count is a numeric variant of that explicit threshold.

rejected_candidates.candidate: Field Hospitals cannot save warriors when the Keep is simultaneously destroyed
rejected_candidates.reason: Q27 removes all simultaneous pieces before triggers and Q08 explicitly requires the Keep destination. This named combination does not create a separate timing rule.

rejected_candidates.candidate: Base loss and sympathy removal trigger order within a battle
rejected_candidates.reason: Q69 explicitly assigns removal-trigger order to the affected side. Combining it with two existing Alliance consequences is not novel.

rejected_candidates.candidate: Bird cards can foil ambushes in any nonbird clearing
rejected_candidates.reason: Matching foil and bird wildness are explicitly keyed; a suit-specific example is a mechanical recombination.

rejected_candidates.candidate: Coalition partner cannot be the target of an enemy-only nonbattle effect
rejected_candidates.reason: Q59 expressly says coalition partners are not enemies; the source glossary defines enemy globally. Applying that definition to Strike is a mechanical recombination.

rejected_candidates.candidate: Quest deck exhaustion or unavailable discard-card handling invented beyond the assigned Law
rejected_candidates.reason: No additional procedure is given by the authoritative source. The audit does not invent one.

rejected_candidates.candidate: Expanded factions, second Vagabond, hirelings, landmarks, bots, other maps/characters or Advanced Setup
rejected_candidates.reason: These are expressly outside the assigned review scope.

checked_passages.actual_answer_evidence: The answers give card/Law/Learning-to-Play precedence, follow-both-before-faction priority, absolute cannot, and current-player fallback; Q69 supplies the explicit battle-order exceptions.

The answer distinguishes public hand count from restricted contents, inspectable face-up piles from unsearchable shared deck, nonbinding agreements, instructed card transfers and absence of consent requirements.
The answers expressly state Birdsong-Daylight-Evening order, clockwise handoff, start-before-other-effects and end-after-other-effects boundaries.
March cannot be interrupted between moves, and the final turn step locks out ordinary actions while retaining explicitly timed end actions.
Maximum possible piece manipulation, no proxies, nonwaived costs/prerequisites, shortage allocation, simultaneous removals before triggers and full Decree completion are all in actual answers.
The answer expressly preserves faction ownership and excludes items from faction ownership/pieces.
Forced actions preserve the acting faction rules/restrictions and battle decisions; allied movement is explicitly forced movement.
The answers give top-level immediate reshuffle, optional bird wildness including matching-card groups, mandatory substitution for forced nonbird give/discard, and prohibition on reverse substitution.
The answers distinguish noncraftable ambush/dominance cards and give their play/activation/suit-spending uses.
The answer gives play-area destination and forbids spending/using those cards as hand without explicit instruction.
Answers use linking paths and clearing adjacency/suits, explicitly exclude rivers as normal paths, and address the Winter exception to forest division.
Building placement needs an open slot; occupied ruin slots cannot be built over; last explored item removes the ruin and opens its slot.
The answer gives touching-clearing adjacency without crossing a printed path and forest-forest adjacency across exactly one printed path.
The answer counts warriors/buildings, compares each other player, excludes tokens/pawns, and gives ordinary no-rule ties.
Immediate 30-VP victory is explicitly before action/phase/turn completion; simultaneous ties use clockwise proximity including the current player.
Answers give one VP per removed enemy building/token, defender eligibility, normal printed crafting VP, and the Eyrie exception.
The answers state own Daylight, ten VP, score-marker removal/no further points, all four suit win conditions and start-of-Birdsong timing; Vagabond coalition exception is separate.

Answers identify matching crafting icons rather than card suit, clearing-defined crafting-piece suit, any-suit question-mark icon, once-per-turn piece use and the Vagabond exception.
Answers resolve/discard immediate cards, take corresponding item from map supply to Crafted Items box, award printed VP normally and prohibit crafting absent items.
Answers retain persistent effects in play and prohibit identical effects already in the play area.
The answer states a positive-size group, one linking path to one adjacent clearing, rule at either endpoint and unrestricted repeated movement of pieces.
The actual answer requires attacking warriors/pawn and an enemy in the same clearing, does not require rule, and excludes coalition partners as enemies.
The answer gives matching defender ambush, matching attacker foil, two immediate unfoiled hits, discard and immediate end if attacking warriors/pawns are gone.
Answers give before-roll/roll/after-roll order, attacker choice when both sides have effects, high/low dice and warrior caps with Alliance/Vagabond exceptions.
Answers cover uncapped extra hits, defenseless extra attacker hit, Vagabond sword-based defenselessness and ignored-hit subtraction from the total.
Answers give one piece per hit, taking-side removal choices, warriors before buildings/tokens, taking-side removal-trigger ordering and Vagabond item-damage replacement.
Answers give random starting player/seating, zero scores, three-card hands, two-player dominance removal, four ruins, exact item supply, dice and faction letter setup order.
The answer gives recommended two/three/four-player Reach totals, all four base faction values and the permissive 17+ guideline.
The answer explicitly identifies workshop crafting first in Marquise Daylight.
Answers give Keep placement exclusion versus legal movement, failed enemy replacement, Field Hospitals payment/location, and unrebuildable Keep/no hospital destination after removal.
The answer gives 25 warriors/eight wood, corner Keep, all-but-opposite-corner garrison, all three starting buildings near Keep and five remaining of each type on tracks.
The answer gives Birdsong wood per sawmill, finite supply and Evening base draw plus uncovered bonuses then discard to five.
Answers give craft-first then three actions plus bird expenditures outside actions, battle availability, two-move March, once-per-turn Recruit and shortage allocation.
The answer gives ruled target/open slot, leftmost type, displayed wood cost, connected ruled wood network, wood removal then building placement and uncovered-space VP.
The answer gives a matching sawmill-clearing card for one wood there.
Answers identify roost crafting before Decree, Eyrie tie rule requiring an Eyrie piece, one VP instead of printed item VP and retention of extra crafting VP effects.

The answer gives empty-hand emergency draw, mandatory one-or-two Decree additions/at-most-one bird and no-roost recovery in a legal fewest-warrior clearing.

Answers give sympathy-token crafting and defensive high/low reversal while retaining warrior caps.
Answers separate supporters from hand, permit self-inspection, restrict use to suit, implement five-with-no-base/unlimited-with-base capacity and discard incoming overflow.

Answers distinguish face and damage, require ready undamaged action items, route gained/face-up items appropriately, move exhausted track items to Satchel and cap each track at three.

The answer expressly compares allied-warrior hits against item hits in that battle, defers hostility until battle end, exempts equality and overrides normal first-warrior hostility.

Answers give first-warrior hostility, own-turn battle-only Infamy excluding the triggering warrior, extra boot only for hostile warriors, Aid inability to reverse Hostile and coalition reset to Indifferent.
The answers restrict entry into forests to Slip while allowing normal Move out into adjacent clearings and apply forest adjacency.
Answers give character choice, any-forest pawn, three public shuffled quests, one randomized R item per ruin, S-marked character starting items/destinations and Indifferent relationships.
Answers give Refresh based on tea already face up, then three more; optional free Slip even Hostile, outbound restriction immunity, proper adjacency and distinct forest Rest semantics.
Answers give normal boot/hostile-boot movement, no normal forest entry, sword-exhaustion battle cost and difference between exhausted passive swords and usable action swords.
The answer gives torch cost, ruin in current clearing, face-up item, VP only if taking an item and removal/open slot after last item.
Answers give any ready-item exhaustion, matching clearing card to a player with faction pieces there, optional crafted-item reward, legal Aid without a reward and legal Aid to a Hostile faction.
The answer gives clearing-matching quest, two listed item exhaustions, completed-quest placement, either same-suit completed-quest VP including current or two drawn cards, then replacement quest.
The answer gives crossbow cost and priority to that enemy warrior, allowing other faction pieces only when that enemy lacks warriors; no Strike Infamy.
Answers give hammer Repair preserving face, hammer-per-crafting-icon and single-clearing icon match, plus all three applicable character actions/costs.
Answers give forest-only damaged-item Rest face up, coin-track draw then discard to five, last-step Satchel+Damaged capacity six+two per bag track item and permanent excess removal.

Operational glossary consequences are in keyed answers: adjacency, draw/deck, faction/enemy/item identity, matching, hand versus play area, default place/remove sources/destinations, random Steal, replace completion, show, spend/discard and swap ignoring place/move restrictions. Pure shape/name definitions introduce no additional action procedure.
All inventory limits relevant to base action legality and faction setup are covered by the actual supply/setup answers; bibliographic/component-count trivia creates no distinct procedural branch.
The answer expressly says Autumn/Fall has no special rule and Winter river divides forests as paths do.
The answer lists each base character starting inventory and torch action: random Steal, matching/bird Day Labor and three-item Hideout followed immediately by Evening.
The back-page setup/craft/move/battle reminder repeats numbered procedures already checked; it introduces no new scoped rule.

stopping_rule_challenge.common_rules_result: No distinct omitted core procedure found. The additions Q67-Q77 actually supply the immediate victory, battle eligibility/order, ignored hits, item destinations, crafting eligibility, Mobilize, Eyrie Evening, sword cost, turn handoff and damage-location rules; these are present in the key, not merely mapped.
stopping_rule_challenge.faction_rules_result: No distinct omitted base-faction or map/character procedure found after checking action costs, target prerequisites, track routing, damage/readiness, allies, hostility, coalitions and ordered phase steps.
stopping_rule_challenge.conclusion: The final two zero-addition passes survive this independent challenge. This is saturation under the stated novelty standard, not a claim to enumerate every legal combination.
